candidates.source_body_excerpt: Time is running out to see documents and artefacts which have been hidden in Rochdale’s archives. The display currently on show in the town centre is the result of Rochdale Local Studies and Co-operative Heritage Trust’s project Unlocking Collections which has seen 10 volunteers search through documents, donations and purchases which reflect the town’s heritage. The collection is now on display at Rochdale Local Studies and at the Square Gallery on Rochdale Town Hall Square. Rochdale Local Studies Centre shared on Facebook: “Over the course of the project, our volunteers have explored and researched local archive collections, working with artist and facilitator Mitch Robinson to create artwork inspired by the stories they discovered. “Their work is now on display throughout September in the Square Gallery on Rochdale Town Hall Square, bringing these local stories to life for the wider community. “A huge congratulations and thank you to all our wonderful volunteers for their creativity, time and hard work.” READ MORE: Town hall is perfect setting for Rochdale’s first Steampunk festival Your Trust shared: “These documents have grown over time through generous donations and purchases and the resources reflect the innovative and radical town of Rochdale.

candidates.source_summary: Alleged victim in Rochdale grooming trial has received £89,000 in compensation, jury told Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The trial of six men accused of the historic sexual abuse of three girls in Rochdale heard that one of the alleged victims has received £89,000 in compensation. Girl B was allegedly exploited in the mid 2000s. Girl A was said to have been abused in the same period. While the alleged abuse of another, Girl C, allegedly began in the late 1980s. The trio were ‘groomed', 'manipulated' and became 'sex slaves', often being forced to have sex ‘with multiple men on the same day, in filthy flats and houses’, prosecutors allege. Click here to hear the latest from Manchester's courts in our newsletter Tahir Rashid, 55; Mohammed Saleem, 47; Sucklane Shah, 47; Amjad Mahmood, 54; Iftaq Hussain, 46; and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face. As the trial at Minshull Street Crown Court continued, Girl B was cross-examined in court by Mr Rashid’s barrister, Ayaz Qazi KC. Mr Qazi claimed that Girl B had given ‘limited details’ about Mr Rashid. He put it to her: “I’m going to suggest that the reason you are able to give very limited details about [Mr Rashid] is because they are details you have picked up from [Girl A].” Girl B replied: “No, because if she remembered more she would have told me more, if I was making it up I could have said more. I’m only saying what I remember.” Jurors heard that Girl A and Girl B lost touch but began messaging each other again as adults. Mr Qazi referenced messages from Girl A which mentioned compensation. Asked whether she had received compensation, Girl B said: “I got £20,000 which was from social services, and then I got £69,000 from the CICA [Criminal Injuries Compensation Authority].” Asked for the total figure she received, Girl B said: “It would have been £89.000.” Girl B claims she was raped by Mr Rashid at his home in Rochdale. Mr Qazi put it to her: “You didn’t visit that Bamford house did you?” Girl B replied: “I did.” The KC continued: “And you didn’t engage in any sexual activity with him at that house, did you?” Girl B replied: “I did.” Mr Qazi asked the witness: “Is it your position that apart from that occasion at the VIPER [video identification} parade, you have never had any face to face contact with [Girl A]?" “No, I haven’t," the witness responded. Girl B said she had exchanged messages with Girl A, but that this was not just about ‘this case and this operation’, and that ‘there was other things we spoke about’. Mr Rashid, of Hudsons Walk, Rochdale, denies 12 counts of rape; three counts of indecent assault; and one count of assault by penetration. The charges include allegations against all three complainants. Mr Saleem, of Bradley Smithy Close, Rochdale denies eight counts of rape allegedly committed against Girl A. Mr Shah, of Crawford Street, Rochdale, denies two counts of rape allegedly committed against Girl B. Mr Mohammed, of Merefield Street, Rochdale, denies four counts of rape; and one count of assault by penetration. The charges include allegations against Girl A and Girl B. Mr Hussain, of Hey Street, Rochdale, denies three counts of rape allegedly committed against Girl A. Mr Mahmood, of Channing Street, Rochdale, denies 11 counts of rape, two counts of indecency with a child, two counts of assault by penetration and one count of indecent assault. The charges include allegations against Girl A and Girl B. Proceeding .

candidates.source_summary: Plans to turn delipidated former storage units into flats have been thrown out over issues with bin collections.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to turn delipidated former storage units into flats have been thrown out over issues with bin collections. Ghulam Hadhar applied to Rochdale Council for permission to create seven self-contained apartments at 24a Baron Street, on the edge of Rochdale town centre. Planning documents describe the U-shaped building overlooking a courtyard as being is in a state of disrepair. They add: “The proposed development will bring a mostly disused existing building and wider site into a suitable and sustainable use which is currently open to crime, dumping and anti-social behaviour, and could become an eyesore over time. “It is positioned in a prominent location in the town centre, and an opportunity has arisen where investment can be made to bring the building to a suitable functional use and where it would not have a negative impact on the surrounding area. “Minimal changes are made externally to the building. The proposal involves the removal of existing roller shutters to doors and windows and the insertion of new windows and doors at ground and first-floor level which would include sandstone head and cills to match the existing. “The courtyard area would provide good-sized outdoor amenity space retained to the rear of the site for future residents.” The plans include creating a bin storage area with the bins to be collected from Oldham Road, but issues have been raised over rights of way.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Fireworks will return to the region’s biggest park as the borough gets ready for Bonfire Night. As well as fireworks in Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton, celebrations will return to Heaton Park for the first time in seven years. Manchester City Council last held firework celebrations in its parks in 2019 but they will return this year on Saturday, November 7. The council has decided not to include bonfires, with the entertainment focusing instead on free family-friendly fireworks to “bring communities together”. Another change will see two different displays at the parks, with a reduced-noise display held at 5pm for families and SEND audiences, followed at 8pm with the main fireworks displays. Cllr Garry Bridges, Leader of Manchester City Council said: “Residents tell us how important it is to create opportunities for our communities to come together and celebrate. “Our fireworks display is exactly one of those events that bridge culture and background – and so it’s fantastic to bring back these free community displays that give families, friends and neighbours a shared experience.” Earlier in the week, on Monday, November 2, Rochdale Council will be holding the first of its three Bonfire Night events, with a firework display and family funfair at at Bowlee Community Park in Middleton.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Planners have given their blessing for the site of a former church to become homes. Zest Eco applied to Rochdale Council to build seven new houses on land at Egerton Street — the former New Jerusalem Church — in Middleton, which was founded before 1886 and was demolished by 2012. In planning documents, Zest said: “The proposal delivers seven three-bedroom family dwellings, each with private gardens and dedicated parking. “This form of development responds directly to the identified need for family housing rather than higher-density flat accommodation. “Full planning permission is sought for the erection of seven 2.5-storey three-bedroom townhouses with rear dormers, solar panels, associated parking, private gardens, landscaping and vehicular access via a new dropped kerb from Egerton Street. “The proposal regenerates a vacant brownfield site to deliver family housing within an established residential neighbourhood, respecting local character, safeguarding neighbouring amenity and providing safe and efficient access arrangements.” There were five objections to the plans, including a loss of on-street parking for existing residents, overdevelopment of the site and the loss of green space. candidates.source_title: Rochdale 2-0 Oldham - Sky Sports
candidates.source_summary: Rochdale lifted themselves off the foot of the League Two table with a 2-0 win against Oldham in their Greater Manchester derby.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Rochdale lifted themselves off the foot of the League Two table with a 2-0 win against Oldham in their Greater Manchester derby.

The home side took the lead just seven minutes in. Charlie Tasker and Jonny Smith combined down the right, and Tasker's low delivery in behind the retreating Oldham defence was swept into the roof of the net by Dan Moss.

Oldham frontman Mike Fondop missed a gilt-edged chance on 25 minutes, sliding the ball wide of the post with an open goal at his mercy after a mistake from Dale stopper Nils Ramming, who had his pocket picked by Keenan Appiah-Forson.

The visitors continued to press forward after the interval, Kane Drummond's delivery across the face of goal eluding Fondop and substitute Calum Kavanagh.

Dale delivered a sucker punch when they doubled the lead on 62 minutes. Latics keeper Matt Hudson's kick towards the halfway line was met by Baba Adeeko, who headed the ball forward for Dajaune Brown to advance into the penalty area, side-step Donervon Daniels and slam a firm drive into the bottom corner.

candidates.source_title: Ian Watson praises Rochdale players after beating Oldham - Ayr Advertiser
candidates.source_summary: Ian Watson praises Rochdale players after beating Oldham Ayr Advertiser
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale boss Ian Watson praised his players for adapting to the demands of the Greater Manchester derby clash against Oldham following their 2-0 win at the Crown Oil Arena. Dan Moss’ seventh-minute opener eased the tension around the stadium, fans having called for Watson’s head in the previous home fixture, a 4-1 loss against Gillingham. Oldham spurned several chances before Dajaune Brown doubled the lead for Dale in the 62nd minute. The win lifted Watson’s men off the foot of the League Two table and secured bragging rights over their near neighbours. “Derby days bring a lot of tension and nerves and probably suit a different style than the one we like to play, these games are full of chaos,” said Watson. “But I thought we adapted and found a way to win the game incredibly well. Today was just about getting a result for the fans and for the club. The scoreboard was all that mattered. “The performance wasn’t where we want it to be, but derby days are almost an isolated case where you just need the scoreboard right and to get a good feeling around the club. “I’m incredibly proud of the boys. We’d spoken all week about what this game means to the fans and how much we wanted to run and duel with the opposition to show how much it means to us, and I thought the players did that.” In between Dale’s goals, Oldham had created several openings. Mike Fondop headed a good chance over and then fired wide with an open goal at his mercy after a mistake from Dale goalkeeper Nils Ramming. Oldham manager Micky Mellon was bitterly disappointed his side were unable to reward the travelling supporters and accepted responsibility for the result would fall on his shoulders.

candidates.source_title: Oldham Athletic left to rue missing gilt-edged chances in derby defeat at Rochdale - theoldhamtimes.co.uk
candidates.source_summary: Oldham Athletic left to rue missing gilt-edged chances in derby defeat at Rochdale theoldhamtimes.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Oldham Athletic suffered derby day defeat for the first time in a decade in the league. Latics looked comfortable in possession in the opening exchanges, albeit without doing anything to hurt Rochdale. But they were stung in the eighth minute when a cross from the right was flicked on in the box and Oldham looked to make amends from that early defensive lapse and carved out a number of openings. But they failed to capitalise on any of them. Just five minutes after falling behind Kane Drummond whipped a good ball into the box, Mike Fondop climbed to meet it but could not keep his free header down. Rochdale then struggled to deal with an Ollie Norburn corner that he sent to the far post, the ball was only half cleared but Gus Scott-Morriss' header was too tame to trouble goalkeeper Nils Ramming. But the worst of the misses came just before the half-hour. Keenan Appiah-Forson did well to put Ramming under pressure and force the keeper to lose control of the ball, it rolled for Fondop, but the striker put his low shot narrowly wide with an open goal at his mercy.

candidates.source_title: Heywood’s ‘Willy Wonka’ moment as gala photos look very different to flashy AI advert - Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_summary: A Heywood gala has been compared to Glasgow’s infamous Willy Wonka experience after photos from the event showed a considerably smaller set-up than the colourful promotional artwork.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The Heywood Community Gala advert depicted large fairground rides and promised a family funfair, live music and DJs, street food and children's entertainment.

The event was advertised as running from Friday 18 September until Sunday 20 September at The Pig and Whistle in Heywood.

Its promotional image generated by AI depicts large fairground rides, performers, balloons and crowds alongside a list of attractions including licensed bars, face painting, children's characters and games and information stalls.

Photos supplied from the venue on Saturday morning show around eight gazebos outside. The large fairground rides depicted in the promotional artwork are not visible in the photographs.

The difference has prompted comparisons on Facebook with the Willy Wonka-themed experience in Glasgow which attracted widespread attention in 2024 after visitors complained that the reality did not match its elaborate promotional imagery.

A Facebook page called Cameron Boland - Scam Event Watch & Awareness has been criticising the Heywood event and previously alleged it was a scam. The page can be found here; https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100095319109710

In its latest post, the page claimed Cameron Boland had said some of the biggest costs involved in the gala were security, staging and infrastructure, and production and entertainment.

The page alleged there was no stage and claimed performers were appearing on a rug between tables. It also questioned the security arrangements.

Those claims have not been independently verified; however, there have been multiple events captured by this page.

The same page published a warning on 9 September telling traders not to pay money upfront for stalls and made further allegations concerning previous events linked to Mr Boland.

A very similar event by the same organiser was forced to be cancelled by Salford City Council and GMP, the same 3-day event on 18, 19 and 20 August.

Those allegations have not been established as fact.

The photographs show activity taking place at The Pig and Whistle on Saturday but cannot establish everything available at the venue during the three-day event.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Resilient Roch is an innovative flood and climate resilience programme delivered through a partnership between Rochdale Borough Council and the National Flood Forum. Funded by the Flood and Coastal Innovation Programme (FCIP), the project seeks to improve resilience among households and communities vulnerable to flooding, particularly in disadvantaged and diverse neighbourhoods. Resilient Roch is an innovative flood and climate resilience programme delivered through a partnership between Rochdale Borough Council and the National Flood Forum. Funded by the Flood and Coastal Innovation Programme (FCIP), the project seeks to improve resilience among households and communities vulnerable to flooding, particularly in disadvantaged and diverse neighbourhoods. Rather than relying on conventional consultation methods, Resilient Roch adopts a relationship-first approach that builds trust through long-term engagement with residents, community organisations, schools and local stakeholders. By integrating flood resilience with wider issues such as housing, health, wellbeing and climate awareness, the programme strengthens community preparedness and adaptation. Rochdale has a long history of flooding, including major events such as the 2015 Storm Eva floods, which affected hundreds of homes and businesses and exposed wider social vulnerabilities. Research highlighted that flood risk disproportionately affects disadvantaged communities, particularly where poor housing, low incomes, limited insurance uptake and institutional distrust intersect. Traditional engagement and consultation approaches often struggle to reach those most vulnerable to flooding, including marginalised communities, non-English speakers and socially isolated residents. The project aimed to increase flood and climate resilience across vulnerable communities while addressing barriers that limit participation. Key objectives included improving flood literacy, supporting the uptake of property flood resilience measures, strengthening financial resilience through insurance awareness, encouraging community ownership of flood preparedness and increasing understanding of climate risks. The programme also sought to develop stronger partnerships between residents, community organisations, local authorities and other stakeholders to create lasting resilience and community capacity. Resilient Roch adopted a place-based, relationship-led model of engagement that prioritised trust, local knowledge and long-term community presence. The project built on more than a decade of collaboration between Rochdale Borough Council and the National Flood Forum (NFF), enabling the programme to draw on established community trust, local knowledge and existing relationships rather than starting engagement from scratch.

Rochdale Council will also receive support through the Local Youth Transformation programme to strengthen leadership, train its workforce and build lasting local partnerships. The new Young Futures Hub will provide young people in Rochdale aged 10 to 18 — and up to 25 for those with SEND — with access to seamless, holistic support. Alongside open-access sport, creative activities and trusted youth workers, the hub will connect young people with mental health support, skills and training, routes into employment and crime prevention services. The expansion forms part of the Government’s National Youth Strategy, Youth Matters, launched by Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy in December, 2025, and co-produced with 14,000 young people through the State of the Nation survey. candidates.source_summary: Delivering for Rochdale, from our streets to the world stage inyourarea.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: When I was a lad growing up on a council estate in Spotland, the idea that a Rochdale MP might one day sit round a table in government would have seemed far-fetched. For nearly two hundred years this town sent its members to Parliament without a single one of them holding a departmental ministerial post. That changed this summer, and I still feel the weight of it. Being appointed Minister for Early Education by Prime Minister Andy Burnham is the honour of my working life. But a title only matters if it delivers something real for the people back home. So this month I want to tell you what that job has actually meant for Rochdale. Much of my brief is about giving children the best possible start in life, and over the holidays I saw exactly what that looks like on the ground. At KYP, at BACP, at Aspire 2 Inspire in Greenbank, and with the Rochdale Nigerian Community Association in Broadfield Park, I watched local youngsters get a proper meal and a day full of sport, science and fun through the Government's Holiday Activities and Food programme. As the minister now responsible for that programme across the whole country, there is a real pride in seeing our own community groups make it work so well right here. I also visited the Best Start Family Hub on Derby Street in Heywood, one of seventeen hubs across our borough that support families from bump and birth through those crucial early years. That support makes a real difference to families across our borough, and I will fight to expand it. None of this is charity. It is the difference a Government makes when it decides that where you are born should never decide how far you get. That same principle runs through the £20m of Pride in Place money coming to Smallbridge, Hurstead and Belfield over the next ten years. This is your money to shape, so I have been out and about hearing what local people actually want from it, from Haroon's chippy on Stevenson Square to the team at Cohen's Chemist. The whole point of this fund is to give local people a real say, and I intend to make sure that promise is kept. Ministerial red boxes have not kept me away from the things that make our town what it is. Over the past few weeks I have cheered on the Hornets, welcomed the veterans of Get Together After Serving as they opened their brilliant new cafe opposite Rochdale AFC, joined the Armed Forces Breakfast Club at the Flying Horse for Parachute Regiment veteran Brian Lamb's 90th birthday, and stood in a packed Town Hall Square as OMD paid tribute to the town where they began. Rochdale at its very best. This week my work takes me a good deal further afield. I am in Paris representing the United Kingdom at UNESCO's Digital Learning Week, where education ministers from more than twenty-five countries are wrestling with one of the biggest questions of our age: how we make the most of artificial intelligence in our classrooms without losing what makes teaching human.

It works extremely well in the Octagon’s intimate space with Rachana Jadhav’s big, impressive set spreading across about a third of the auditorium. The three main acting areas encompass a central one that transforms from the Khan family’s kitchen to their business - a fish and chip shop, and briefly to their front parlour; another to represent their back yard, complete with the “shed” that bundle of nervous energy, youngster Sajit retreats to and “sunbathes” on top of in his protective but rather smelly parka. and another, representing the base of a factory chimney, with a balustrade where the brothers can be together, away from mum and dad. Director Kash Arshad summarises the plot as being “the experience of being brought up in a Muslim household, with a white British mother and a Pakistani father, who ran his own business, with kids who felt not British enough to be British nor Pakistani enough to be Pakistani.” Overbearing with self-importance dad George Khan is trying to rule his family for what he believes is the best according to religion and tradition. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Oldham Athletic face their first derby of the season on Saturday, looking to protect a record that has stood for almost a decade. Not since October 2016 have Latics suffered a league defeat to Rochdale. Matty Lund's 40th minute goal was enough to secure bragging rights for Latics' rivals at Spotland. Since then, however, Oldham have come out on top, winning four of their nine league meetings and drawing five. Rochdale did come out on top when the two went head-to-head in the Football League Trophy in December 2018 at Spotland, although the hosts left it late. Latics were reduced to 10 men when Mohammed Maouche saw red six minutes into the second half. The game remained goalless until the 90th minute when Rochdale were awarded a penalty which Joe Rafferty converted, before Daniel Adshead made it 2-0 in stoppage time. Of their 66 competitive meetings, in all competitions, 62 of them have been in the league, with Latics winning the majority with 24. There have been 22 draws, while Rochdale have come out on top in 16 meetings.
